runner: artifacts/forensics/night7-corner2-bbfoxy-20260927/corners.sh in the worktree (sha256 feef1e11f9319ce53240a47f4d0c319340dd5ed1d8a220ba34df9dfee8f8125d), the first corner runner's controls (airplane mode, do-not-disturb and USB stay-on for the runs, restored after; the game log streamed for the office seed), run under tools/device/device-lock-exec.py with CUE_HELPER_LOCK_DIR set to the main checkout's captures/cue-helper/locks so the serial lease is the one every other session and the Cue Helper MCP take. Each night-run is bounded at 1800 s (SIGINT, whose EXIT trap releases the HID and returns the phone to an observed title). It stops the cohort on a missing title after any run, on two consecutive device faults (an excluded run, or a run that hit the bound), and on a counted night that ends with no executor terminal.
grading: after each run, python3 tools/device/run-timeline.py captures/<run>.mp4 --json writes artifacts/runs/<run>/timeline.json (defaults: 2 fps, 1.5 s dwell), and npm run evidence -- pack <run> --replace re-packs the run with it, as the first corner cohort's packs were; the result is npm run evidence -- cohort on this file

rules.counted: a run counts once the campaign observes state=night; its outcome is the executor terminal (sixam or gameover) cross-checked by the video terminal grade
rules.win: executor terminal sixam and video TERMINAL clear
rules.death: gameover; cause taken from the per-cycle ledger and the video, survival time from the video
rules.excluded: a run refused or aborted before state=night is not counted and is re-run in its slot as rNNb; the reason is reported. Two consecutive device faults stop the cohort (the session's standing rule), so a slot gets at most rNN and rNNb
rules.invalid: a counted run whose night was interrupted by something outside the game (a notification, the operator touching the phone, a USB drop) is reported as invalid with the evidence, and re-run in its slot
rules.noTuning: no knob, anchor, bundle or harness change inside the cohort; a harness fault stops the cohort rather than being patched mid-way. A counted night that ends with no executor terminal is such a fault: it is reported UNKNOWN as it stands, never re-graded from the video by hand, and never re-run in its slot
